findings.reason: Independently inspected the authentic original standalone tile and frozen/current source. The long rational parametrization obscures two different identifications: antipodal boundary pairs form the domain quotient, while three distinct interior points have the same immersion image. A domain-to-target schematic materially clarifies this distinction even though the proof is complete.
findings.action: Added a fenced TikZ schematic and explanatory paragraph in a final Remarks section. It marks paired boundary points a and -a, three interior poles, and three forward arrows under the extended map to a single target 0; explicitly identifies beta: RP^2 -> R^3.

diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: D is the closed complex unit disk; q:D -> RP^2 is the boundary-antipodal quotient (F2). beta:RP^2 -> R^3 is the immersion from Verification 4.1. The displayed map from D to R^3 is the extended P = beta composed with q.
diagram_math_checks.check: Domains and codomains compose correctly; the three arrows are evaluations of the extension, not paths on the immersed surface.

diagram_math_checks.relation: q(a)=q(-a) for a on the boundary
diagram_math_checks.justification: F2 identifies exactly antipodal boundary points in the disk model; a and -a are drawn at opposite boundary locations. No interior points are identified by this quotient.

diagram_math_checks.relation: w_j = r exp(2 pi i(j-1)/3), r=((3-sqrt(5))/2)^(1/3), j=1,2,3, are distinct interior poles
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification 1.1 gives w^3=u_+=(3-sqrt(5))/2 in (0,1). Thus these are its three cube roots of radius r<1, at angles 0,120,240 degrees. Diagram uses proportional schematic coordinates with these angles and radius approximately 0.725 of the disk radius.

diagram_math_checks.relation: x_j=q(w_j) are distinct and beta(x_j)=0 for all three j
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification 3.1 extends P to each pole with value 0; Verification 5.1 states these are distinct projective-plane points because their sphere antipodes lie outside the disk. The three forward arrows converge on one target dot, without identifying source dots.

diagram_math_checks.relation: No global normal side or embedding is depicted
diagram_math_checks.justification: The circle represents the parameter disk only, and the target is a single point in R^3. No Boy-surface outline, normal vector, or crossing/over-under claim is introduced. Verification 1.1–6.1 remains unchanged and independent.
